dct_description_sm:
Shows areas where forest insect pests have damaged or killed trees by defoliation, foliage mining and wood boring.

Tree mortality rarely occurs as the result of one year’s infestation, but from the result of several consecutive years of infestation and other contributing factors affecting weakened trees (e.g., fungal invasion).

The Government of Ontario tracks forest damage events to help proactively manage the detrimental effects to our forests. We monitor the threat and spread of invasive forest pest insect species in Ontario.

The data is also important to the Forest Management Planning process in calculating timber volume loss within affected areas.

Recommendations
Users of the information stored in this data class should be aware that:- The spatial accuracy coarseness of mapped insect damage events. This fact must be considered for any type of comparison with other data-sets (e.g.: Forest Resource Inventory).- Mapped perimeters represent the gross outer perimeter of the event only. As such, the area within this moderate-severe defoliation can also include roads, cultivated areas, small lakes, or burned areas. Areas reported as defoliated may also include patches of different severity classes, and pockets where no damage has occurred.- Insect pest forest defoliation and mortality are mapped as separate events (which may overlap).- Mapped forest mortality is the result of the cumulative damage over several years of infestations and other abiotic/biotic factors. - Data Class accommodates history, and overlaps will exist in consecutive years between insect damage events.- Other than identifying the event's year, the insect pest agent, the extent of damage (perimeter and ranking), no other information stored in NRVIS.
